findings.reasoning: SD identifies cleanly and closes on nothing. Five of the eight compiled pathways bind 1:1 on a shared operative citation — § 23A-3-27 to sd_arrest_expungement, § 23A-3-34 to sd_23a_3_34_auto, §§ 23A-3-35 to 23A-3-37 to sd_diversion, §§ 23A-27-13 to 23A-27-17 to sd_sis_sealing and § 24-14-11 to sd_pardon_24_14_11 — which uses up all five registry tracks and leaves exactly three pathways with no track, matching the +3 delta. The three run on § 23A-27-53, §§ 26-7A-115 to 26-7A-116 and § 26-7A-115.1, none of which appears anywhere in the registry. Neither closure route is available. Variant decomposition would require the target track to carry the authority: sd_sis_sealing lists §§ 23A-27-13, 23A-27-14 and 23A-27-17 and not § 23A-27-53, and the compiled drug route says only that the court must dismiss the original charge — it does not state that the dismissal produces sealing under § 23A-27-17, so treating it as a narrower variant of the SIS track would be an assumption, not evidence. A registry scope restriction is not available either: SD's three stop conditions concern Class 2 misdemeanor limits, non-chapter-24-14 pardons and §§ 22-22-1/22-22-7 teaching licensure, and none names a juvenile or trafficking authority the way WY's tracks name § 14-6-241 and § 6-2-708. What is missing is precisely that: an SD registry track or stop condition naming § 23A-27-53, chapter 26-7A, or § 26-7A-115.1. Recorded unresolved rather than guessed.
